then.text: How's the bike? Squeaking? Good. A squeak means it's got opinions.
Use the bike anywhere with room to ride, and ring the bell at pedestrians. It's the law. In my shop.
Garside sent you? She said you'd have a Stone about you. Go on then, show us.
Ooh, it's smooth. Buxton water, that. A proper Hedge-lay stone. Brambles will fold like deckchairs.
Right. A bike. Nothing fancy, no gears you can't pronounce. Tested in thirty years of Manchester rain.
West of town is Chat Moss, then Liverpool. Flat and soggy. Tell the bog I said hello.

else.text: Bike shop. If it has two wheels and a problem, I'll fix it.
Professor Garside rang ahead. She said you'd show me a Stone. A Brook Stone, to be exact. No Stone, no bike. I don't make the rules, I just enforce them cheerfully.
